To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the economic and technical optimization of an OR-C waste heat recovery unit coupled with a biopower plant is a complex task, which requires a detailed analysis of the market, the technical constraints of the ORC components and the economic constraints related to the investment and operation costs.
subcritical ORC is the most suitable solution in terms of technical and economic performances for the biogas plant considered in this study.
the sub-critical and wet-expansion ORC systems are the most suitable solutions in a real case study of a biogas plant in the Italian region Emilia-Romagna.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (i) the development and implementation of a methodology for the technical and economic optimization of ORC systems for waste heat recovery from a biogas plant; (ii) the analysis of the optimal ORC system in terms of energy savings, pay-back period and profitability.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the wet-expansion architecture is the best solution from both economic and technical points of view, with a pay-back time of about three years, and an electrical efficiency higher than 20%.

, in a real application, wet expansion ORC systems with turbomachinery expanders can be a good solution for a biogas plant in terms of energy saving, but they are not economically feasible in the considered case study.
the optimal solution depends on the economic and technical constraints and the type of expander.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the wet expansion ORC system is the best option in terms of energy savings, economic feasibility and technical reliability, followed by the transcritical ORC and finally the subcritical ORC.
the optimal ORC solution is the trans-critical cycle with a screw expander, followed by the wet expansion cycle with a screw and the wet expansion with a reciprocating expander.
the subcritical ORC with a volumetric expander is the most suitable solution, in terms of economic and technical performances, in the considered application.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal architecture depends on both technical and economic constraints.
wet expansion cycles are more suitable in the case of low temperature sources, while sub-critical ORC systems are the optimal solution for medium-high temperature applications.
, for the considered application, subcritical ORC is the best solution in terms of economic performance, followed by trans-critical and finally wet expansion cycles.
